transcript.text: Thank you, Marisol. Eli, I appreciate you raising that, and I want to be clear that I respect your participation requirement. I have no intention of initiating unscheduled one-to-one confrontations, and I'm fully comfortable with all repair conversations being facilitated by Marisol with at least 24 hours' notice. As for my proposal about the shared template and 48-hour response window, I still think a six-week trial period makes sense — it lets us evaluate whether the arrangement works well in a formalized context before committing to it for the full quarter. But I'd also want to make sure that the 48-hour response window and the facilitated repair process don't conflict with each other in any way. If a handoff response is due within 48 hours but a repair conversation needs 24 hours' notice plus scheduling with Marisol, we should think through how those two timelines interact so neither of us is put in an awkward position. I'd welcome Eli's thoughts on that.

transcript.text: Thank you, Dana, for raising that timeline interaction — it's a really important point. You're right that the 48-hour response window and the 24-hour notice requirement for facilitated repair conversations could create tension if they're not thought through together. Here's my thinking: the 48-hour window applies to routine handoff responses using the shared template — acknowledging receipt, providing context, flagging issues. A repair conversation is a different thing entirely — it's needed when something goes wrong in the handoff process that can't be resolved through the template alone. So I'd suggest we clarify in the plan that the 48-hour window governs standard handoff responses, while repair conversations follow the facilitated process with 24 hours' notice. If a situation arises where a handoff response is due but the issue requires a repair conversation, the response within 48 hours could simply note that a facilitated discussion is being requested, and the actual substantive resolution would happen in the scheduled facilitated session. That way neither of us is pressured into an unfacilitated one-to-one exchange to meet the 48-hour deadline, and the template still gets a timely response. As for the six-week trial period, I'm comfortable with that. It gives us a defined window to evaluate how the formalized arrangement works alongside the facilitated repair process, and we can adjust before committing to the full quarter. Marisol, does that framework make sense to you for documenting both pieces?

transcript.text: Yes, Eli, that framework makes excellent sense to me. Let me summarize what I'm hearing so I can make sure I capture it accurately for the operating plan. First, the shared written handoff template and 48-hour response window would be formally documented for a six-week trial period, during which we evaluate how the arrangement works in its formalized context. Second, the 48-hour window governs standard handoff responses — acknowledging receipt, providing context, and flagging issues through the template. Third, repair conversations are a separate process: they must be facilitated by me, scheduled with at least 24 hours' notice, and no unscheduled one-to-one confrontations between Dana and Eli will occur. Fourth, if a situation arises where a handoff response is due within 48 hours but the issue requires a repair conversation, the response within the 48-hour window can simply note that a facilitated discussion is being requested, and the substantive resolution happens in the scheduled facilitated session. This way, neither of you is pressured into an unfacilitated exchange to meet a deadline, and the template still gets a timely response. Both of you have indicated you're comfortable with this framework. Before I finalize this into the operating plan, is there anything either of you wants to add, clarify, or adjust?
